articles.title: Receita abre consulta a lote residual de R$ 1,2 bilhão do IRPF | G1
articles.standfirst: Lote contempla mais de 412 mil contribuintes que regularizaram pendências ou enviaram declaração em atraso. Pagamentos de serão depositados no dia 30 de setembro.
articles.summary: Lote contempla mais de 412 mil contribuintes que regularizaram pendências ou enviaram declaração em atraso. Pagamentos de serão depositados no dia 30 de setembro.
articles.body:
Receita abre consulta a lote residual de R$ 1,2 bilhão do Imposto de Renda de setembro — Foto: g1

A Receita Federal liberou, a partir das 9h de quarta-feira (23), a consulta ao lote residual de restituição do Imposto de Renda Pessoa Física (IRPF) referente ao mês de setembro de 2026.

Este lote é voltado para os contribuintes que entregaram a declaração de 2026 fora do prazo, corrigiram erros na malha fina ou que tinham direito a resíduos de anos anteriores.

Ao todo, serão distribuídos R$ 1.265.846.221,42 para 412.186 contribuintes . O crédito bancário será depositado diretamente nas contas indicadas no dia 30 de setembro .

Do montante total de R$ 1,2 bilhão, mais de R$ 466 milhões serão destinados a pessoas que possuem prioridade legal garantida por lei.

A divisão dos pagamentos prioritários ficou definida da seguinte forma:

Idosos acima de 80 anos: 9.250 restituições;

Idosos entre 60 e 79 anos: 59.722 restituições;

Contribuintes com deficiência física, mental ou moléstia grave: 7.341 restituições;

Profissionais do magistério (cuja maior fonte de renda seja a educação): 19.699 restituições.

Além disso, o lote beneficia 281.609 contribuintes que, embora não tenham prioridade por lei, receberam preferência por terem utilizado a declaração pré-preenchida ou optado pelo recebimento via PIX.

Outros 34.565 contribuintes sem prioridade legal também foram incluídos neste lote.

Na 2ª Região Fiscal da Receita Federal, que engloba o Pará e outros estados, um grupo de 23.489 contribuintes receberá o total de R$ 47.397.459,70 .

Somente no estado do Pará, o órgão vai pagar R$ 23.482.323,43 para 10.977 pessoas . O valor em solo paraense está dividido entre as seguintes delegacias da Receita:

Belém e região metropolitana: R$ 16.470.410,24 destinados a 6.354 contribuintes;

Marabá : R$ 4.214.201,63 destinados a 3.005 contribuintes;

Santarém : R$ 2.797.711,56 destinados a 1.618 contribuintes.

Como consultar a restituição do IRPF 2026?

Para saber se o seu nome está na lista de pagamentos deste lote, o processo é simples e pode ser feito pela internet. Veja como:

Acesse o site oficial da Receita Federal ( );

Em seguida, selecione "Consultar minha restituição".

Para uma verificação mais detalhada, o contribuinte pode acessar o extrato de processamento da declaração no portal e-CAC.

Caso identifique alguma pendência ou erro que o tenha retido na malha fina, é possível enviar uma declaração retificadora diretamente pelo sistema para corrigir as informações.

A consulta também está disponível por meio do aplicativo da Receita Federal para tablets e smartphones (Android e iOS).

Por motivos de segurança, a Receita Federal realiza o pagamento da restituição exclusivamente na conta bancária de titularidade do próprio contribuinte.

Se houver qualquer divergência de dados ou se a conta informada estiver inativa, o depósito não será efetuado.

Caso ocorra algum problema no crédito, o valor ficará disponível para resgate por até um ano no Banco do Brasil. Nesse caso, o cidadão deverá solicitar o reagendamento do pagamento.

Como reagendar o pagamento no Banco do Brasil:

Pela internet: Acesse o portal do BB especializado em IRPF (

0800-729-0088 (exclusivo para deficientes auditivos).

No momento do reagendamento, é obrigatório informar o valor exato da restituição e o número do recibo da declaração do IRPF 2026.

Se o contribuinte não resgatar o dinheiro no banco dentro do prazo de 12 meses, será necessário fazer um pedido de pagamento diretamente pelo Portal e-CAC.

Basta acessar o menu Declarações e Demonstrativos > Meu Imposto de Renda > Solicitar restituição não resgatada na rede bancária e preencher os dados solicitados.

articles.title: Cathie Wood Just Made Another Big Bet on Rocket Lab
articles.summary: ARK Invest bought another $25 million of Rocket Lab shares as the company approaches its 97th Electron launch and prepares for its next major growth phase.
articles.body:
Rocket Lab USA ( RKLB , Financials ), is drawing fresh attention after Cathie Wood's ARK Invest bought another 359,612 shares worth about $25.1 million, adding to its recent purchases of the space company.

The latest buying came across ARK's Innovation, Autonomous Technology & Robotics, and Space Exploration & Innovation ETFs. Earlier this month, ARK also bought 200,303 Rocket Lab shares worth about $12.8 million.

The timing is notable. The Wall Street Journal recently reported that SpaceX has stopped selling new Falcon 9 rideshare missions, while some companies are struggling to secure launches beyond 2028. If launch capacity remains tight, Rocket Lab could have more opportunities to win customers.

Rocket Lab is also preparing for its 97th Electron launch on Sept. 25. The mission will carry a StriX satellite for Japanese Earth-imaging company Synspective into low-Earth orbit and would mark the company's fourth Electron launch in 25 days.

The bigger piece of Rocket Lab's growth story remains Neutron, its planned larger launch vehicle. Cantor Fitzgerald analyst Andres Sheppard has a $122 price target and sees Neutron's first launch as a key catalyst, alongside Rocket Lab's planned acquisition of Iridium.

TipRanks says 14 analysts rate RKLB Buy and three rate it Hold, with an average price target of $109.47.

The next catalyst is Friday's Electron launch, followed by further progress toward Neutron's first flight.

articles.title: Why Oracle's force majeure notice is freaking out AI bulls
articles.body:
Oracle ( ORCL ) has placed bets across the AI ecosystem, and a new complication could pose problems for the industry.

The tech beast has issued a force majeure notice for its 2.45-gigawatt site in Doña Ana County, N.M., named Project Jupiter, according to a Bloomberg report.

The site is tied to the Stargate initiative with OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) and SoftBank ( SFTBY ), with OpenAI as the customer. The notice, reportedly sent to the project's developer, private credit player Blue Owl Capital ( OWL ), is an attempt to delay payments if Project Jupiter fails to go online in 2028.

"Project Jupiter remains on our planned schedule. We are fully committed to New Mexico and confident in our path forward," Oracle vice president Michael Egbert said in a statement to Yahoo Finance. "Force-majeure notices are commonplace in developments of this scale and are often used to preserve contractual rights among project partners. They do not, by themselves, establish a project delay or change delivery expectations."

Oracle stock tanked 4% on the news in Thursday's trading. The development cast a dark cloud over the AI space, sending shares of Nvidia ( NVDA ), AMD ( AMD ), and Micron ( MU ) lower.

"Oracle is in the most tenuous of cash positions of all the major hyperscalers," KeyBanc analyst Jackson Ader said. "These types of issues might spread, but Oracle does feel it more acutely than its larger, more cash-rich peers."

Issues spreading is the key concern here, as Oracle has inked scores of deals and taken on enormous amounts of debt to fund its artificial intelligence ambitions. Any disruption to its carefully constructed AI mosaic could make it much harder for Oracle financially, and that means others in the AI space could feel it too.

"By leasing the data centers and getting financing from third parties sometimes the cash payments of the project might be committed to on timelines that do not match the real-world project timeline," Ader continued. "That seems to be what is happening here. Payments might be due on a chronological timeline, but the revenue generation is up to the whims of the complex real-world logistics."

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Power Players with Brian Sozzi podcast, and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team. Follow Sozzi on X @BrianSozzi , Instagram , and LinkedIn . Tips on stories? Email brian.sozzi@yahoofinance.com.

articles.title: Meta is banking its future on its Muse AI agent — and winning user trust
articles.summary: Muse is Meta's vision for its future.
articles.body:
Meta ( META ) CEO Mark Zuckerberg laid out his vision for the company's future during its Meta Connect conference on Wednesday, and it's all about Muse .

The social media giant's new AI agent has quickly jumped to the top of both Apple's App Store and Google's Play Store, and, according to Zuckerberg, millions of people are using it.

During Connect, Meta chief AI officer Alexandr Wang demonstrated a number of use cases for Muse, ranging from the mundane, like scheduling meetings, to more impressive feats like negotiating better rates for cable service and making purchases across multiple services.

Meta is also bringing Muse to its next-generation Meta VR Glasses , allowing you to speak to a digital avatar of your agent, as well as to its Muse Charm. A handheld, purpose-built device, the Muse Charm lets you interact with your Muse agent without a smartphone or smart glasses.

The company said it will make money from Muse by taking a small cut on transactions made via the agent.

"We struggle over the big details and the small ones. It's not always easy. Sometimes, whole years are hard, but we build because this is who we are. And the centerpiece of our vision for what we're building is Muse," Zuckerberg said during his keynote.

"I expect that Muse is going to grow into the personal super intelligence that billions of people around the world are going to use to accomplish their goals and improve their lives," he said.

On the Pressure Points podcast, Deepwater Asset Management managing partner Gene Munster explained that Meta's push into the AI agent space will have major implications for its business, such as reducing its reliance on algorithms that serve up content based on a user's past browsing habits.

"This, to me, is … a huge deal when it comes to how they're presenting the technology and how they're going to drive adoption," Munster said regarding the shift toward Muse versus the prior influence-dominated social media space.

But if Meta is going to win over users beyond early adopters and AI boosters, it will need to convince people that it takes privacy and security seriously.

The company clearly recognizes that. A portion of the Connect keynote was dedicated to explaining how Meta secures user data.

"We designed state-of-the-art privacy and security into all these systems from the beginning," Zuckerberg said.

"We built the Muse Secure VM to keep your information on your own secure virtual machine, and soon we are also going to release the Muse Confidential VM so that even Meta won't be able to see that information," he added.
